summary: When someone must pay from his land, the mishnah tells which kind of land is used: the best, the middle, or the poorest.

chunks.en: For damages, they judge the value using the best land,
chunks.st: The court appraises land of superior quality [iddit] for payment to injured parties.

chunks.en: and a lender collects from the middle land,
chunks.st: And a creditor collects his debt from the debtor’s intermediate-quality land.

chunks.en: and a woman's kesubah from the poorest land.
chunks.st: And payment of a woman’s marriage contract is collected from her husband’s inferior-quality land.

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says:

chunks.en: a woman's kesubah also comes from the middle land.
chunks.st: Payment of a woman’s marriage contract is also collected from intermediate-quality land.

summary: A debt is not taken from land the borrower already sold to others while he still has land of his own. From orphans, it is taken only from the poorest land.

chunks.en: We do not collect from property that was sold to others when
chunks.st: Payment of a debt or other obligation is not collected from liened property that has been sold to a third party when

words.note: Land that was sold, but still tied to a debt.

chunks.en: there is property that is still free,
chunks.st: the debtor still has unsold property,

chunks.en: even if it is the poorest land.
chunks.st: even when this unsold property is inferior-quality land.
chunks.stMore: The creditor cannot collect his debt from liened property that the debtor has sold to another person as long as the debtor is still in possession of other property, even if the remaining assets are inferior to those to which the creditor would otherwise have been entitled.

chunks.en: We do not collect from the property of orphans,
chunks.st: If one who owed money died and his children inherited his property, the father’s debt can be collected from the property of the orphans

chunks.en: except from the poorest land.
chunks.st: only from inferior-quality land.

summary: To help the world, some payments may not be taken from land that was already sold to others. Also, a person who returns a lost object does not have to swear.

chunks.he: אֵין מוֹצִיאִין לַאֲכִילַת פֵּרוֹת וּלְשֶׁבַח קַרְקָעוֹת
chunks.en: We do not take from sold property for eaten fruit or for land that got better,
chunks.st: The court does not appropriate liened property that has been sold to a third party for the consumption of produce or for the enhanced value of land.
chunks.stMore: If one appropriated a field and sold it, and the buyer worked the land, enhanced it, and grew produce on it, and then the initial owner from whom the field had been stolen took back the land and the produce from the buyer, compensating him only for his expenses, then the buyer may go back to the seller, i.e., the robber, and collect his losses. He can collect the purchase price of the field even from property that the robber sold to another person. By contrast, the value of the produce and the enhancement in the value of the field, which resulted from his actions, may be collected only from the robber’s unsold property.

chunks.en: or for feeding a man's wife and daughters, from sold property,
chunks.st: And similarly, payment for the sustenance of a man’s wife and daughters cannot be collected from his liened property.
chunks.stMore: One of the stipulations included in a marriage contract is that after the husband dies, his widow and daughters are entitled to sustenance from his estate. This sustenance cannot be collected from husband’s liened property that has been sold to another person, but only from his unsold property inherited by his heirs.

chunks.en: to make the world better.
chunks.st: All of these enactments were made for the betterment of the world.

chunks.en: And someone who finds a lost object
chunks.st: And it was further instituted that one who finds a lost item and returns it to its rightful owner is

chunks.en: does not have to swear,
chunks.st: not required to take an oath that he did not keep any part of the lost item for himself.

chunks.en: to make the world better.
chunks.st: This ordinance was also instituted for the betterment of the world.

summary: This mishnah teaches about a guardian who takes care of orphans, and about people who ruin someone else's food or a korban on purpose or by mistake.

chunks.en: Orphans who are taken care of by a homeowner,
chunks.st: With regard to orphans who are living with a homeowner
chunks.stMore: who takes care of all their needs and affairs, even if neither their father nor the court officially appointed him to this task,

chunks.en: or whose father chose a guardian for them,
chunks.st: or if their father appointed a steward [apotropos] for them,

chunks.en: he must take maaser from their fruit.
chunks.st: this person is obligated to tithe their produce.

chunks.en: A guardian whom the orphans' father chose
chunks.st: With regard to a steward who was appointed by the orphans’ father,

chunks.en: must swear. If the beis din chose him,
chunks.st: when he returns all of the property to the orphans upon their reaching adulthood, he takes an oath that he took nothing of theirs for himself. By contrast, if the court appointed him

chunks.en: he does not have to swear.
chunks.st: to serve as a steward for them, then he is not required to take such an oath.

chunks.en: Abba Shaul says,
chunks.st: Abba Shaul says:

chunks.en: it is the other way around.
chunks.st: The matters are reversed.
chunks.stMore: A steward appointed by the court takes an oath, but a steward appointed by the orphans’ father is not required to do so.

chunks.en: Someone who makes food tamei, or mixes terumah into it, or pours wine for avodah zarah, by mistake,
chunks.st: With regard to one who renders another’s food ritually impure, or one who mixes teruma with another’s non-sacred produce, or one who pours another’s wine as a libation before an idol, in each of these cases causing the other a monetary loss, if he acted unintentionally,

words.en: and one who mixes in terumah
and one who pours for avodah zarah

chunks.en: does not have to pay. On purpose,
chunks.st: he is exempt from paying for the damage. If he acted intentionally,

chunks.he: חַיָּב. הַכֹּהֲנִים שֶׁפִּגְּלוּ בַמִּקְדָּשׁ מְזִידִין, חַיָּבִין:
chunks.en: he must pay. Kohanim who spoil a korban in the Beis HaMikdash on purpose must pay.
chunks.explain: They ruined it by thinking wrong thoughts while bringing it.
chunks.st: he is liable to pay. If priests disqualified an offering with improper intention in the Temple, by expressing, while sacrificing the offering, the intention of sprinkling the blood of the offering, burning its fats on the altar, or consuming it, after its appointed time, and they did so intentionally, they are liable
chunks.stMore: to pay the value of the offering to its owner, who must now bring another offering.

words.note: A korban ruined by wrong thoughts about when it will be eaten.

summary: Rabbi Yochanan ben Gudgeda told the Sages four halachos he had received, including two rules made to help people do teshuvah and to help the mizbeach.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yochanan ben Gudgeda testified
chunks.st: Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Gudgeda testified before the Sages

chunks.en: about a girl who cannot hear whose father married her off,
chunks.st: about the case of a deaf-mute woman who was married off by her father
chunks.stMore: when she was a minor, so that her marriage took effect by Torah law.

chunks.en: that she can leave the marriage with a get.
chunks.st: He said that she can be released from her marriage through a bill of divorce,
chunks.stMore: whether as a minor or after she reaches adulthood. Although as a deaf-mute woman she is not legally competent to give her consent, the divorce is effective because divorce does not require the woman’s consent.

chunks.he: וְעַל קְטַנָּה בַת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנִּשֵּׂאת לְכֹהֵן,
chunks.en: And about a young daughter of a Yisrael who married a Kohen,
chunks.st: And similarly, he testified about the case of the minor daughter of a non-priest who was orphaned from her father and then married off to a priest
chunks.stMore: by her mother or brother, so that her marriage took effect by rabbinic law.

chunks.en: that she may eat terumah,
chunks.st: He said that nevertheless she may partake of teruma,
chunks.stMore: although by Torah law it is prohibited for one who is not in a priestly household to partake of teruma.

chunks.en: and if she dies,
chunks.st: And furthermore if this girl dies,

chunks.en: her husband inherits from her.
chunks.st: then her husband inherits her estate.
chunks.stMore: It is not said that because the validity of the marriage is by rabbinic law and not Torah law he is not entitled to inherit from her.

chunks.en: And about a stolen beam that was built into a big building,
chunks.st: And Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Gudgeda further testified about a stolen beam that was already built into a large building [bira],

chunks.en: that the owner gets only its value,
chunks.st: that the victim of the robbery receives only the value of the beam but not the beam itself,

chunks.en: to help people who do teshuvah.
chunks.explain: The thief does not have to break the building to return it.
chunks.st: due to an ordinance instituted for the penitent.
chunks.stMore: By Torah law, a robber is obligated to return any stolen item in his possession, provided that its form has not been altered. If one stole a beam and incorporated it into a building, then by Torah law he would have to destroy the building and return the beam. In order to encourage repentance, the Sages were lenient and allowed a robber to return the value of the beam.

chunks.he: וְעַל חַטָּאת הַגְּזוּלָה שֶׁלֹּא נוֹדְעָה לָרַבִּים,
chunks.en: And about a stolen chatas that many people did not know was stolen,
chunks.st: And lastly, Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Gudgeda testified about a sin-offering that was obtained through robbery but that was not publicly known to have been obtained in that manner.

chunks.en: that it does bring kaparah,
chunks.st: He said that it effects atonement for the robber who sacrifices it,

chunks.en: to help the mizbeach.
chunks.st: for the benefit of the altar, as will be explained in the Gemara.

summary: In the time of the war, cruel men called sikarikon took fields from their owners. This mishnah tells when someone who buys such a field keeps it, and how the owner gets paid.

chunks.he: לֹא הָיָה סִיקָרִיקוֹן בִּיהוּדָה בַהֲרוּגֵי מִלְחָמָה.
chunks.en: There was no sikarikon law in Yehudah during the time of those killed in the war.
chunks.explain: A sikarikon took fields from people by scaring them.
chunks.st: The law of Sicarii [Sikarikon] did not apply in Judea in the time that people were being killed in the war.

words.note: A cruel man who took fields by threats.

chunks.en: From the time of those killed in the war and on,
chunks.st: From the time that people were being killed in the war and onward,

chunks.en: there was the sikarikon law there.
chunks.st: the law of Sicarii did apply there.

chunks.he: כֵּיצַד. לָקַח מִסִּיקָרִיקוֹן וְחָזַר וְלָקַח מִבַּעַל הַבַּיִת,
chunks.en: How so? If he bought from a sikarikon, and then also bought from the owner,
chunks.st: What is this law of Sicarii? If one first purchased land from a Sicarius, who extorted the field from its prior owners with threats, and afterward the buyer returned and purchased the same field a second time from the prior landowner,

chunks.en: his buying does not count.
chunks.st: his purchase is void.
chunks.stMore: The prior owner of the field can say that he did not actually mean to sell him the field.

chunks.en: From the owner, and then he bought from a sikarikon,
chunks.st: By contrast, if he first acquired the field from the prior owner and afterward he returned and purchased the same field from a Sicarius,

chunks.en: his buying stands.
chunks.st: his purchase stands.

chunks.en: If he bought from the husband and then
chunks.st: Similarly, if one first purchased from the husband the rights to use a field belonging to his wife, and

chunks.en: bought from the wife,
chunks.st: afterward he returned and purchased the same field from the wife,
chunks.stMore: so that if the husband were to predecease or divorce her, the purchaser would then own it fully,

chunks.en: his buying does not count.
chunks.st: his purchase is void.
chunks.stMore: The woman can claim that she did not wish to quarrel with her husband and to object to the transaction but that in truth she did not agree to the sale.

chunks.he: מִן הָאִשָּׁה וְחָזַר וְלָקַח מִן הָאִישׁ,
chunks.en: From the wife, and then he bought from the husband,
chunks.st: By contrast, if he first acquired the field from the wife, and afterward he returned and purchased the same field from the husband,

chunks.en: his buying stands.
chunks.st: his purchase stands.

chunks.en: This is the first mishnah.
chunks.st: This is the initial version of this mishna.

chunks.en: The beis din that came after them said,
chunks.st: Later, the court of those who came after the Sages who composed that mishna said:

chunks.en: one who buys from a sikarikon gives the owner a quarter.
chunks.st: With regard to one who purchased a field from a Sicarius, he must give the prior owner one-fourth of the field’s value.

chunks.en: When? When the owners cannot buy it themselves.
chunks.st: When does this apply? At a time when the prior owner is unable to purchase the field himself.

chunks.en: But if they can buy it,
chunks.st: But if he is able to purchase it himself,

chunks.en: they come before anyone else.
chunks.st: he precedes anyone else.

chunks.en: Rebbi set up a beis din, and they voted,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi later convened a court, and they counted their votes and determined

chunks.en: that if the field stayed with the sikarikon
chunks.st: that if the field remained before, i.e., in the possession of, the Sicarius for

chunks.en: twelve months,
chunks.st: twelve months,

chunks.en: whoever buys it first
chunks.st: whoever first purchases the field

chunks.en: gets it, but he gives the owner a quarter.
chunks.st: acquires possession of it, but he must give the prior owner one-fourth of the field’s value.

summary: A person who cannot hear or speak may buy and sell things by hand signs. Young children may also buy and sell small things.

chunks.en: A cheresh may make signs and answer by signs.
chunks.st: The following enactments were also made for the betterment of the world: A deaf-mute may express his wishes through gestures [romez];
chunks.stMore: that is to say, he can signal that he wishes to buy or sell a certain item, and the purchase or sale is valid.

chunks.en: And ben Beseira says,
chunks.st: And similarly he may respond to others through gestures;
chunks.stMore: that is to say, he can signal that he agrees to a transaction initiated by another party, and the transaction is valid. And ben Beteira says:

chunks.en: he may move his lips, and answer by moving his lips,
chunks.st: Signals are not necessary, as even if he expresses his wishes to buy or sell through lip movements [kofetz] or responds to others through lip movements,

chunks.en: for things that can be moved. Young children:
chunks.st: the transaction is valid. These halakhot apply to transactions involving movable property.
chunks.stMore: It was similarly enacted that

chunks.en: their buying is buying and their selling is selling, for movable things.
chunks.st: a purchase made by young children [paotot] is a valid purchase, and a sale made by them is a valid sale. These halakhot apply to transactions involving movable property.

summary: The Rabbis made some rules to keep peace among people, like the order of aliyos to the Torah and not taking things that a person almost owns.

chunks.he: וְאֵלּוּ דְבָרִים אָמְרוּ מִפְּנֵי דַרְכֵי שָׁלוֹם.
chunks.en: And these are things they said to keep peace.
chunks.st: Having mentioned a series of enactments instituted by the Sages for the sake of the betterment of the world, the Gemara continues: These are the matters that the Sages instituted on account of the ways of peace,
chunks.stMore: i.e., to foster peace and prevent strife and controversy:

chunks.en: A Kohen reads first,
chunks.st: At public readings of the Torah, a priest reads first,

chunks.en: and after him a Levi, and after him a Yisrael,
chunks.st: and after him a Levite, and after him an Israelite.

chunks.en: to keep peace.
chunks.st: The Sages instituted this order on account of the ways of peace,
chunks.stMore: so that people should not quarrel about who is the most distinguished member of the community.

chunks.en: We put the eruv in the old house,
chunks.explain: The same house where it was always put.
chunks.st: Similarly, the Sages enacted that a joining of courtyards is placed in an old house where it had regularly been placed

chunks.en: to keep peace.
chunks.st: on account of the ways of peace,
chunks.stMore: as will be explained in the Gemara.

chunks.en: A pit that is closest to the water channel
chunks.st: The Sages enacted that the pit that is nearest to the irrigation channel
chunks.stMore: that supplies water to several pits or fields

chunks.en: gets filled first,
chunks.st: is filled first

chunks.en: to keep peace.
chunks.st: on account of the ways of peace.
chunks.stMore: They established a fixed order for the irrigation of fields, so that people would not quarrel over who is given precedence.

chunks.en: Traps for animals, birds, and fish:
chunks.st: Animals, birds, or fish that were caught in traps
chunks.stMore: are not acquired by the one who set the traps until he actually takes possession of them. Nevertheless, if another person comes and takes them, it

chunks.en: taking from them counts as stealing,
chunks.st: is considered robbery

chunks.en: to keep peace.
chunks.st: on account of the ways of peace.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: it is real stealing.
chunks.st: This is full-fledged robbery.

chunks.en: Something found by a cheresh, a shoteh, or a child:
chunks.st: Similarly, a lost item found by a deaf-mute, an imbecile, or a minor
chunks.stMore: is not acquired by him, since he lacks the legal competence to effect acquisition. Nevertheless, taking such an item from him

chunks.en: taking it counts as stealing,
chunks.st: is considered robbery

chunks.en: to keep peace.
chunks.st: on account of the ways of peace.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: it is real stealing.
chunks.st: This is full-fledged robbery.

chunks.en: A poor man who knocks olives off the top of an olive tree:
chunks.st: If a poor person gleans olives at the top of an olive tree
chunks.stMore: and olives fall to the ground under the tree, then taking those olives

chunks.en: taking what is under him is stealing,
chunks.st: that are beneath it is considered robbery

chunks.en: to keep peace.
chunks.st: on account of the ways of peace.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: it is real stealing.
chunks.st: This is full-fledged robbery.

chunks.en: We do not stop poor
chunks.st: One does not protest against poor gentiles

chunks.en: non-Jews from taking leket, shikchah, and pe'ah,
chunks.explain: These are parts of the harvest left for the poor.
chunks.st: who come to take gleanings, forgotten sheaves, and the produce in the corner of the field, which is given to the poor [pe’a],
chunks.stMore: although they are meant exclusively for the Jewish poor,

words.note: Stalks that fall during the harvest.
Bundles that were forgotten in the field.
The corner of the field left for the poor.

chunks.en: to keep peace.
chunks.st: on account of the ways of peace.

summary: A woman may lend tools to a neighbor who may not be careful with mitzvos, but she may not help her do the aveirah. All this is to keep peace.

chunks.he: מַשְׁאֶלֶת אִשָּׁה לַחֲבֶרְתָּהּ הַחֲשׁוּדָה עַל הַשְּׁבִיעִית,
chunks.en: A woman may lend to her friend who is suspected about Shemitah fruit,
chunks.st: A woman may lend utensils to her friend who is suspect with regard to eating produce that grew in the Sabbatical Year after the time that such produce must be removed from the house and may no longer be eaten.
chunks.stMore: The utensils that she may lend her include:

words.note: The seventh year, when fields rest.

chunks.en: a sifter, a sieve, a millstone, and an oven,
chunks.st: A winnow, a sieve, a mill, and an oven.
chunks.stMore: Lending her such utensils is not considered aiding in the commission of a transgression.

chunks.he: אֲבָל לֹא תָבֹר וְלֹא תִטְחַן עִמָּהּ.
chunks.en: but she may not sort or grind with her.
chunks.st: But she may not select the grain from the chaff or grind wheat with her,
chunks.stMore: i.e., she may not actively assist her in the performance of a sin.

chunks.he: אֵשֶׁת חָבֵר מַשְׁאֶלֶת לְאֵשֶׁת עַם הָאָרֶץ,
chunks.en: The wife of a chaver may lend to the wife of an am ha'aretz
chunks.st: The wife of a ḥaver, one who is devoted to the meticulous observance of mitzvot, especially the halakhot of ritual purity, teruma, and tithes, may lend the wife of an am ha’aretz, one who is not scrupulous in these areas,

words.note: A person very careful with tumah, terumah and maaser.
An am ha'aretz is someone not careful with these mitzvos.

chunks.en: a sifter and a sieve,
chunks.st: a winnow and a sieve,

chunks.en: and she may sort, grind, and sift with her,
chunks.st: and she may even select, grind, and sift with her.

chunks.en: but once she pours the water in,
chunks.st: But once the wife of the am ha’aretz pours water into the flour,
chunks.stMore: thereby rendering it susceptible to ritual impurity,

chunks.en: she may not touch it with her,
chunks.st: the wife of the ḥaver may not touch anything with her,

chunks.he: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין מַחֲזִיקִין יְדֵי עוֹבְרֵי עֲבֵרָה.
chunks.en: because we may not help people who do aveiros.
chunks.st: because one may not assist those who commit transgressions.

chunks.en: And all of these they said only
chunks.st: And all of the allowances mentioned in the mishna were stated only

chunks.en: to keep peace.
chunks.st: on account of the ways of peace.

chunks.en: And we may help non-Jews who work in Shemitah,
chunks.st: And one may assist gentiles who work the land during the Sabbatical Year,

chunks.en: but not Jews,
chunks.st: but one may not assist Jews who do this.

chunks.en: and we greet them with shalom,
chunks.st: Similarly, one may extend greetings to gentiles

chunks.en: to keep peace.
chunks.st: on account of the ways of peace.
